items.t: Complex Life on Earth May Not Have Appeared Without Tall Mountains
items.sum: As Earth's surface area grew, weathering fed more nutrients into Earth's ancient oceans. This eventually resulted in more oxygen, making Earth more habitable. New research identifies two ancient mountain growth spurts on Earth that directly preceded two of Earth's oxygenation events. The researchers say that taller mountains encouraged habitability and led to complex life.

items.t: This is the First Time Astronomers Have Seen One of These Stellar Mergers
items.sum: Some binary stars end up sharing a common envelope of gas, as the primary star draws material away from its companion. The envelope exerts drag on the stars and they can spiral toward each other. In some cases, this creates an eruption or explosion called a luminous red nova. For the first time, astronomers got to observe one of these in real time.

items.t: The Simons Observatory is Online and Surveying the Cosmic Microwave Background

items.t: Black Holes and Their Mysterious Bright Structures Explained
